OVI.spoken: Column density N is the sum over cells of the ion density times the path length; the O VI density is the hydrogen density times the solar oxygen abundance times the metallicity times the O VI fraction. This cell: {{n}} ions per cubic centimetre over {{dl}} kiloparsecs gives N of ten to the {{N}} per square centimetre.

val.html: τ0​=0.00×100←N=0.00×100cm−2,b=0.00×100kms−1

sym.html: τ0​=1.4975×10−15b[km/s]​Nfλ[A˚]​​

any.spoken: Optical depth at line centre tau zero equals 1.4975 times ten to the minus 15, times column density N, oscillator strength f and wavelength in angstrom, divided by the width b in kilometres per second. Here tau zero is {{tau0}}, from N of ten to the {{N}} and b of {{b}} kilometres per second.

val.html: V=0.00×100kms−1,b=0.00×100kms−1,a=0.00×100

sym.html: τ(v)=τ0​H(a,bv−V​),a=4πbΓλ​

short.html: V=0.00×100kms−1

any.spoken: The optical depth profile is tau zero times the Voigt function H of a and v minus V over b, with damping parameter a equal to Gamma lambda over 4 pi b. Here the dip sits at {{V}} kilometres per second with width {{b}} and damping parameter {{a}}.

val.html: λ=0.00×100A˚⇒V=0.00×100kms−1vgal​=0.00×100kms−1

sym.html: V=c(λ0​λ​−1)−vgal​

short.html: V=0.00×100kms−1

any.spoken: Velocity V equals the speed of light times the observed over the rest wavelength minus one, minus the galaxy's own velocity. Observed at {{lam}} angstrom, the gas moves at {{V}} kilometres per second relative to the galaxy, whose velocity is {{vgal}} kilometres per second.

F.label: transmitted fraction at the deepest point

val.html: τpeak​=0.00×100⇒Fmin​=0.00×100

sym.html: τtotal​(v)=∑i​τi​(v),F=exp(−τtotal​)

short.html: τpeak​=0.00×100

any.spoken: Optical depths of all cells add, and the transmitted flux F is e to the minus total optical depth. So far the deepest point has optical depth {{taup}}, so the flux there is {{F}} of the light.

val.html: R=0.00×100⇒FWHM=0.00×100kms−1

sym.html: Fobs​=F⊗G,FWHM=Rc​

short.html: R=0.00×100

any.spoken: The observed spectrum is the true spectrum blurred by a Gaussian whose full width at half maximum is the speed of light over the resolving power R. At sharpness R of {{R}} the blur is {{fwhm}} kilometres per second wide.

val.html: S/N=0.00×100⇒σpix​=0.00×100

sym.html: σpix​=S/N5​​(5pixels per resolution element)

short.html: S/N=0.00×100

any.spoken: The noise per pixel is the square root of 5 over the signal-to-noise ratio per resolution element, with 5 pixels per resolution element. At exposure S over N of {{sn}} each pixel scatters by {{sig}} of the continuum.

chi.label: reduced chi squared of the fit

val.html: Na​=0.00×100cm−2χν2​=0.00×100

sym.html: χ2=∑j​σj2​(Fobs,j​−Mj​)2​,Na​=πe2me​c​fλ∫τa​(v)dv​

short.html: Na​=0.00×100cm−2

any.spoken: The fit minimises chi squared, the summed squared difference between the observed flux and the model in units of the noise; the apparent optical depth method turns the area of the dip into a column density. Here N a is ten to the {{Na}} per square centimetre and the reduced chi squared is {{chi}}.
